I have been working this land for fifty years. My body is not what it was, and two of my household members spend most of their time working in the city now, so I cannot count on them much during planting and harvest. I must manage things that I can handle mostly by myself, or with hired help at peak times.

My 9 mu I will divide the way I always have — 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation that feeds us and earns steady cash, and 3 mu of cotton because the cotton price has been acceptable and I know this crop well. Cotton is hard work at harvest, but I will hire day laborers for picking like I always do.

For the wheat, I will plant in October using the local improved variety that the seed shop recommends — it performs well and resists rust. I apply fertilizer in two shots: base dressing before planting, and topdress at jointing. I irrigate at sowing, jointing, heading, and grain filling — four times, that is what this dry Hebei winter requires. Wheat needs protecting from aphids and powdery mildew so I will spray twice.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize immediately. I use hybrid seed — yields are much better than what my father used. Maize here does not need as much water as wheat; two or three irrigations is enough. I spray once for borer and once for weeds.

Cotton goes in April. I will use an improved variety. Cotton needs the most attention — I spray four times through the season for bollworm and aphids. I irrigate three times. Cotton is the crop that worries me most with my age, but the income is worth it for 3 mu.

I use rotary tillage for wheat and maize — it is faster and saves my back. For cotton fields I do a deeper plough in spring to break the hardpan.
